description: You are a calculus professor creating 3D course materials for a Calculus II unit on solids of revolution. Using GeoGebra's 3D Graphics view, create an interactive visualization demonstrating the solid formed by rotating the curve f(x) = sqrt(x) over the interval [0, 4] around the x-axis. The visualization must include: (1) the original curve in the 3D coordinate system, (2) the surface of revolution (the resulting paraboloid surface, created using GeoGebra's parametric Surface command), (3) a slider controlling a moveable cross-sectional plane at position x = a, showing the circular cross-section at that x-value (radius = sqrt(a)), and (4) a text display showing the computed volume from 0 to the slider value a using the disk method formula V = pi * integral(x, 0, a) = pi*a²/2. The exact total volume for [0,4] is 8*pi ≈ 25.13. Save as 'solid_revolution.ggb' in ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/
